findings.title: Validator has DB write side effect
findings.body: In lib/validators/email_validator.rb line 13, EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) which increments match_count and saves the record. Validation methods can run multiple times per request (valid?, save, forms, specs), so a single signup attempt can inflate match_count/last_match_at many times and performs a write inside a read-only validation. It also means merely checking validity mutates data, breaking expectations around transactions and making stats unreliable.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, bypassable
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb line 12, should_block? does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw value. User emails are case-insensitive (downcased via Email.downcase elsewhere) but this lookup and the uniqueness validation on line 5 have no downcasing/normalization. An attacker blocked as bad@spammers.org can sign up as BAD@spammers.org or with whitespace/case variants and bypass the block, and duplicate BlockedEmail rows differing only by case can be created.

findings.title: Non-atomic counter increment with unchecked save
findings.body: In app/models/blocked_email.rb lines 14-16, should_block? does record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = Time.zone.now; record.save. This is a read-modify-write race that loses counts under concurrent signups, should use atomic increment/counter update. Return value also ignores save failure, so save validations/callbacks can fail silently while still reporting block/do_nothing.

findings.title: Shared mutable array on controller prototype
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 17, rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) is defined as a property on the object passed to extend. In Ember, mutable objects defined this way are shared across all instances of the controller. Rejected emails from one signup modal session leak into other instances/users of the modal instead of being per-instance state, which should be initialized in init.

findings.title: Wrong dependent key for rejected emails array
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js line 96, emailValidation depends on rejectedEmails.@each but rejectedEmails holds plain strings pushed via pushObject. @each only observes properties on array members, not membership of primitives, so pushing a newly rejected email does not invalidate the computed property. The dependency should be rejectedEmails.[] (or rejectedEmails.length). As written the client may still show the email as valid until accountEmail changes.
